lessons.subject: Maths
lessons.title: Rounding large numbers and decimals
lessons.intention: We are learning to round to estimate and check calculations.
criteria: I can round whole numbers to the nearest 1000, 10 000 and 100 000.
I can round decimals to the nearest whole number, 1 and 2 decimal places.
I can estimate an answer that suits the problem.

steps.start: Round 4 682 to the nearest 1000. How do you know?
steps.teach: Use number lines for large numbers and for decimals (3·46 → 3·5 → 3). Estimate 598 × 4 as 600 × 4. Talk about when to round up (buying enough paint).
steps.practise: Rounding to 100 and 1000, then Estimating answers.
steps.check: Round 56 349 to the nearest 10 000 and 7·286 to 2 decimal places.

lessons.home: Estimate the shopping bill before you get to the till.
lessons.vocab: round, nearest, estimate, decimal place, approximately
lessons.understand: When is rounding useful, and when do you need the exact number?
lessons.lookFor: Gives sensible examples: estimating a shopping total vs. paying the exact amount.

lessons.subject: Maths
lessons.title: Place value to a million
lessons.intention: We are learning to read, write and order numbers to 1 000 000.
criteria: I can read, write and order whole numbers to 1 000 000.
I can explain what each digit is worth.
I can add and subtract multiples of 10, 100 and 1000.

steps.start: Read 305 061 aloud. What is the 5 worth?
steps.teach: Use a place value chart to a million. Partition 482 350. Order five large numbers. Add 3000 to 67 400.
steps.practise: Hundreds, tens and ones, then build bigger numbers on the chart.
steps.check: Write 'two hundred and six thousand and forty' in digits.

lessons.home: Read populations or prices of houses and cars.
lessons.vocab: million, thousand, digit, value, place, partition
lessons.understand: Is 300 000 bigger than 299 999? How can you tell without counting?
lessons.lookFor: Compares from the biggest place value first.

lessons.subject: Maths
lessons.title: Decimals to three places
lessons.intention: We are learning what each digit is worth in decimals.
criteria: I can read, write and order decimals to three places.
I can explain the value of tenths, hundredths and thousandths.
I can partition decimals, as in 3·6 = 3 ones and 6 tenths = 36 tenths.

steps.start: Show 0·5 and ½ on a number line. Are they the same?
steps.teach: Extend the place value chart past the decimal point. Order 0·45, 0·405 and 0·5. Partition 3·6 in different ways.
steps.practise: Decimal fractions.
steps.check: Which is larger, 0·7 or 0·65? Why?

lessons.home: Compare prices and times in a race to the hundredth of a second.
lessons.vocab: decimal point, tenths, hundredths, thousandths
lessons.understand: Which is bigger, 0.4 or 0.35? Why?
lessons.lookFor: Explains 0.4 is 4 tenths and 0.35 is 3 tenths and 5 hundredths, so 0.4 is bigger.

lessons.subject: Maths
lessons.title: Adding and subtracting large numbers and decimals
lessons.intention: We are learning to add and subtract whole numbers and decimals.
criteria: I can add and subtract whole numbers to 1 000 000.
I can add and subtract decimals to two places.
I can choose a mental or written method and explain it.

steps.start: What is 4·5 + 2·7? How did you do it?
steps.teach: Model a written method lining up place values, then with decimals (lining up the point). Compare with a mental method for 3 000 − 1 998.
steps.practise: Adding and taking away bigger numbers.

lessons.home: Add up the receipt and check the total.
lessons.vocab: add, subtract, method, decimal point, total, difference
lessons.understand: Why do the decimal points need to line up?
lessons.lookFor: Explains digits of the same value must be added together.

lessons.subject: Maths
lessons.title: Multiplication and division facts, and ×÷ 10, 100, 1000
lessons.intention: We are learning to use all the times tables and to multiply and divide by 10, 100 and 1000.
criteria: I can use multiplication and division facts to 10 × 10.
I can multiply and divide whole numbers and decimals by 10, 100 and 1000.

steps.start: Quick-fire 6, 7, 8 and 9 times tables.
steps.teach: Use known facts to work out others (7 × 8 = 7 × 4 doubled). Use a place value chart for 3·45 × 100 and 560 ÷ 1000.
steps.practise: 6, 7, 8 and 9 times tables, Division facts, then Multiplying and dividing by 10 and 100.

lessons.home: Practise one times table a day, out loud, for five minutes.
lessons.vocab: multiply, divide, product, quotient, factor
lessons.understand: What is 3.5 × 10? Why doesn't "add a zero" work here?
lessons.lookFor: Says 35, explaining each digit becomes ten times bigger.

lessons.subject: Maths
lessons.title: Multiplying by 2 digits and dividing with decimal answers
lessons.intention: We are learning to multiply by two-digit numbers and divide by a single digit.
criteria: I can multiply whole numbers by two-digit numbers.
I can multiply decimals by a single digit.
I can divide by a single digit, giving decimal answers, as in 43 ÷ 5 = 8·6.

steps.start: What is 23 × 10? And 23 × 2?
steps.teach: Model 23 × 12 as 23 × 10 + 23 × 2, then with a grid or written method. Show 43 ÷ 5 as 8 remainder 3, then 8·6.
steps.practise: Work through a set of 6 calculations on paper, checking with estimates.
steps.check: Work out 34 × 15 and 27 ÷ 4.

lessons.home: Work out costs for several of the same item.
lessons.vocab: multiply, product, divide, remainder, decimal
lessons.understand: Estimate 38 × 21 first. Is your answer close?
lessons.lookFor: Rounds to 40 × 20 = 800 and uses it to check.

lessons.subject: Maths
lessons.title: Order of operations
lessons.intention: We are learning the order to do calculations in.
criteria: I can apply the correct order of operations, including brackets, in multi-step calculations.

steps.start: Is 2 + 3 × 4 equal to 20 or 14?
steps.teach: Explain the order: brackets, then multiply and divide, then add and subtract. Work through examples with and without brackets.
steps.practise: Solve 8 calculations, then write two of your own with brackets that change the answer.
steps.check: Work out (6 + 2) × 3 and 6 + 2 × 3.

lessons.home: Make up number puzzles with brackets for the family.
lessons.vocab: brackets, order of operations, multiply, divide, add, subtract
lessons.understand: Why does 2 + 3 × 4 not equal 20?
lessons.lookFor: Explains multiplication is done before addition unless brackets say otherwise.

lessons.subject: Maths
lessons.title: Negative numbers
lessons.intention: We are learning about numbers less than zero.
criteria: I can say where negative numbers are used, such as temperatures.
I can order negative numbers and place them on a number line.

steps.start: What happens to the temperature at night in winter?
steps.teach: Draw a vertical number line like a thermometer from −10 to 10. Count back through zero. Order −3, 2, −7, 0. Find differences in temperature.
steps.practise: Negative numbers.
steps.check: Which is colder, −4°C or −1°C? What is 3 less than 1?

lessons.home: Check the weather forecast for temperatures below zero.
lessons.vocab: negative, minus, below zero, temperature, number line
lessons.understand: Which is warmer, −2 °C or −7 °C? Why?
lessons.lookFor: Uses a number line or thermometer: −2 is nearer zero, so warmer.

lessons.subject: Maths
lessons.title: Multiples, factors and primes
lessons.intention: We are learning to find multiples and factors.
criteria: I can find multiples and factors of whole numbers.
I can use them to solve problems.
I can recognise prime numbers.

steps.start: List the first five multiples of 6.
steps.teach: Find all factors of 24 using arrays or factor pairs. Show a prime has only two factors. Use a common multiple to solve a problem (buses every 4 and 6 minutes).
steps.practise: Multiples, factors and primes.
steps.check: List the factors of 18. Is 21 prime?

lessons.home: Find the factors of the house number.
lessons.vocab: multiple, factor, factor pair, prime, common multiple
lessons.understand: Why is 9 not a prime number?
lessons.lookFor: Explains 9 has a factor other than 1 and itself (3).

lessons.subject: Maths
lessons.title: Fractions, decimals and percentages are linked
lessons.intention: We are learning that fractions, decimals and percentages can show the same amount.
criteria: I can show equivalent forms, as in ¾ = 0·75 = 75%.
I can choose the easiest form for a problem and explain why.

steps.start: What is ½ as a decimal? As a percentage?
steps.teach: Use a 100 square: shade 25 squares and write ¼, 0·25 and 25%. Build a table for ½, ¼, ¾, ⅒, ⅕.
steps.practise: Percentages, then Decimal fractions.
steps.check: Write 0·2 as a fraction and a percentage.

lessons.home: Spot percentages on food labels and sales signs.
lessons.vocab: equivalent, fraction, decimal, percentage, per cent
lessons.understand: Show me a half three different ways.
lessons.lookFor: Writes 1/2, 0.5 and 50%, and explains they are the same amount.

lessons.subject: Maths
lessons.title: Percentages and fractions of amounts
lessons.intention: We are learning to find fractions and percentages of amounts.
criteria: I can find simple fractions of a quantity, as in ⅗ of 60.
I can find simple percentages of a quantity and use them, as in a 15% discount.

steps.start: What is ½ of 80? 10% of 80?
steps.teach: Find ⅕ of 60 then ⅗ of 60. Find 10% and 5% of £40, then 15%. Work out a sale price.
steps.practise: Percentages, then Halves, quarters and thirds.
steps.check: A £30 game has 20% off. What is the sale price?

lessons.home: Work out sale prices when shopping.
lessons.vocab: fraction of, percentage of, discount, sale price
lessons.understand: Is 25% of 80 the same as a quarter of 80? Why?
lessons.lookFor: Yes: 25% and a quarter are the same proportion.

lessons.subject: Maths
lessons.title: Equivalent fractions and simplest form
lessons.intention: We are learning to make equivalent fractions, simplify and order them.
criteria: I can create equivalent fractions.
I can write a fraction in its simplest form.
I can put common fractions in order.

steps.start: Fold a strip: show ½ = 2/4 = 4/8.
steps.teach: Multiply or divide top and bottom by the same number. Simplify 12/16 using common factors. Order ⅔, ¾ and 5/8 using equivalent fractions.
steps.practise: Equivalent fractions.
steps.check: Simplify 15/20. Put ½, ⅖ and 3/4 in order.

lessons.home: Share a pizza: is 2/8 the same as 1/4?
lessons.vocab: equivalent, simplest form, numerator, denominator, common factor
lessons.understand: Why are 2/4 and 1/2 the same?
lessons.lookFor: Draws or explains the same amount split into more parts.

lessons.subject: Maths
lessons.title: Budgets, best value, profit and loss
lessons.intention: We are learning to manage money, compare costs and work out profit and loss.
criteria: I can do money calculations with all four operations.
I can compare costs and decide what I can afford in a budget.
I understand the benefits and risks of bank cards and paying digitally.
I can work out profit and loss.

steps.start: You have £20 for a party. What would you buy?
steps.teach: Compare two pack sizes to find the better value. Plan a budget with a list of prices. Sell 20 cakes at 50p that cost £6 to make: profit or loss? Talk about card payments and keeping PINs safe.
steps.practise: Counting money, then plan a £25 budget from a price list.
steps.check: Which is better value: 6 for £1·50 or 10 for £2·20?

lessons.home: Compare unit prices together when shopping.
lessons.vocab: budget, afford, best value, profit, loss, bank card
lessons.understand: Is the bigger pack always better value? How can you tell?
lessons.lookFor: Compares the price per item or per gram, not just the total.

lessons.subject: Maths
lessons.title: 12- and 24-hour time and timetables
lessons.intention: We are learning to use 12- and 24-hour time and read timetables.
criteria: I can read and write time in 12- and 24-hour notation and change between them.
I can use timetables and calendars to plan and solve problems.

steps.start: What is 3:45 pm in 24-hour time?
steps.teach: Show a 24-hour clock line from 00:00 to 23:59. Convert times both ways. Read a bus or train timetable: which bus gets there by 14:30?
steps.practise: 12-hour and 24-hour time.
steps.check: Write 18:20 in 12-hour time. Which train arrives first?

lessons.home: Plan a trip using a real bus or train timetable.
lessons.vocab: 24-hour, am, pm, timetable, depart, arrive
lessons.understand: What time is 15:45 on a 12-hour clock? How did you work it out?
lessons.lookFor: Takes 12 off the hours: quarter to four in the afternoon.

lessons.subject: Maths
lessons.title: Durations, units of time, speed and distance
lessons.intention: We are learning to work out durations and how long journeys take.
criteria: I can convert units of time, as in 1¾ hours = 105 minutes.
I can work out durations across hours, in 12- and 24-hour time.
I can choose the right timer and unit, including hundredths of a second.
I can estimate journey times using speed, distance and time.

steps.start: How many minutes in 2½ hours?
steps.teach: Use a time line to find 10:45 to 13:20. Convert hours and minutes. If a car goes 50 km in an hour, how long for 150 km?
steps.practise: How long? Time intervals.
steps.check: A film starts at 18:50 and lasts 1 hour 45 minutes. When does it end?

lessons.home: Time a journey and work out how long it took.
lessons.vocab: duration, hours, minutes, speed, distance, time
lessons.understand: Why can't you subtract 10:50 from 11:20 like ordinary numbers?
lessons.lookFor: Explains there are 60 minutes in an hour, so counts on through the hour.

lessons.subject: Maths
lessons.title: Estimate, measure and convert metric units
lessons.intention: We are learning to estimate, measure accurately and convert units.
criteria: I can estimate using familiar objects.
I can measure length, mass and capacity in the right units.
I can convert between units using decimals, as in 550 cm = 5·5 m.
I can read a range of scales accurately.

steps.start: Estimate the height of the door in metres.
steps.teach: Measure to the nearest mm. Convert km–m–cm–mm, kg–g and l–ml using the place value chart. Read scales with different steps.
steps.practise: Changing units, then Measuring: rulers, jugs and units.
steps.check: Convert 3·009 kg to grams and 2 400 m to km.

lessons.home: Read food labels: how many grams? Convert to kilograms.
lessons.vocab: millimetre, centimetre, metre, kilometre, gram, kilogram, millilitre, litre, convert
lessons.understand: How many millimetres in 4.5 cm? How do you know?
lessons.lookFor: Says 45 and explains there are 10 mm in each centimetre.

lessons.subject: Maths
lessons.title: Perimeter, area and volume
lessons.intention: We are learning to calculate perimeter, area and volume.
criteria: I can calculate the perimeter of straight-sided shapes.
I can calculate the area of squares, rectangles and right-angled triangles.
I can calculate the volume of cubes and cuboids.
I can draw shapes with a given perimeter or area.

steps.start: How could you find the distance round the table?
steps.teach: Find perimeter by adding sides. Find area of a rectangle as length × breadth, and a right-angled triangle as half of that. Build a cuboid with cubes to show length × breadth × height.
steps.practise: Area and perimeter.
steps.check: A rectangle is 7 cm by 4 cm: find its perimeter and area.

lessons.home: Measure a room and work out the area of carpet needed.
lessons.vocab: perimeter, area, volume, square centimetre, cubic centimetre, length, breadth, height
lessons.understand: Can two rectangles have the same perimeter but a different area?
lessons.lookFor: Yes, with an example: 1 × 5 and 2 × 4 both have a perimeter of 12 but areas of 5 and 8.

lessons.subject: Maths
lessons.title: Square, triangular and Fibonacci numbers
lessons.intention: We are learning to explain and use the rules for famous number sequences.
criteria: I can extend square, triangular and Fibonacci sequences and explain the rule.
I can use multiples, square and triangular numbers to make patterns.

steps.start: Build squares with counters: 1, 4, 9… what comes next?
steps.teach: Build square and triangular numbers with counters. Show Fibonacci (each number is the sum of the two before). Find the rule for sequences like 3, 7, 11, 15.
steps.practise: Number patterns.
steps.check: Give the next two numbers of 1, 3, 6, 10 and of 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, with the rule.

lessons.home: Look for Fibonacci spirals in pinecones and flowers.
lessons.vocab: sequence, rule, square number, triangular number, Fibonacci
lessons.understand: Why are they called square numbers?
lessons.lookFor: Shows the number as a square array of dots.

lessons.subject: Maths
lessons.title: Solving simple equations
lessons.intention: We are learning to find an unknown value shown by a letter or symbol.
criteria: I can solve simple equations with one unknown, as in a − 30 = 40 and 4b = 20.

steps.start: I'm thinking of a number. I add 8 and get 20. What's my number?
steps.teach: Use a balance: what you do to one side you do to the other. Solve a + 15 = 40, b − 30 = 40, 4c = 20 using inverse operations.
steps.practise: Missing numbers and signs.
steps.check: Solve 3n = 27 and x − 12 = 19.

lessons.home: Play 'think of a number' puzzles.
lessons.vocab: equation, unknown, solve, inverse, balance
lessons.understand: In 3n + 2 = 14, how do you find n? How can you check?
lessons.lookFor: Undoes the steps in reverse, then puts the value back in to check.

lessons.subject: Maths
lessons.title: Shape properties, nets and circles
lessons.intention: We are learning to describe shapes precisely and link 3D objects to their nets.
criteria: I can use regular, irregular, diagonal, radius, diameter and circumference.
I know the radius is half the diameter.
I can match 3D objects to their nets.
I can draw 2D shapes and represent 3D objects.

steps.start: Is a square a regular shape? Why?
steps.teach: Compare regular and irregular shapes. Measure the radius and diameter of a circle. Unfold a cereal box to see its net, and draw a net for a cube.
steps.practise: 3D objects, then draw two different nets for a cube.
steps.check: A circle's diameter is 12 cm: what is its radius? Which net makes a cube?

lessons.home: Unfold boxes at home to see their nets.
lessons.vocab: regular, irregular, diagonal, radius, diameter, circumference, net
lessons.understand: Will this net fold into a cube? How do you know?
lessons.lookFor: Imagines or tests the folding and spots faces that would overlap.

lessons.subject: Maths
lessons.title: Classifying and measuring angles
lessons.intention: We are learning to name, measure and calculate angles.
criteria: I can classify angles as acute, right, obtuse, straight and reflex.
I can measure and draw angles to within 2°.
I know complementary angles make 90° and supplementary angles make 180°, and can find missing angles.

steps.start: Find an acute and an obtuse angle in the room.
steps.teach: Classify angles. Show how to use a protractor (zero line, which scale). Find a missing angle on a straight line.
steps.practise: Angles and turns, then measure and draw five angles.
steps.check: Measure an angle. Two angles on a straight line: one is 115°, what is the other?

lessons.home: Spot angles in roofs, scissors and clock hands.
lessons.vocab: acute, obtuse, reflex, straight, protractor, degree, complementary, supplementary
lessons.understand: Without measuring, is this angle more or less than 90°?
lessons.lookFor: Compares to a right angle first, then measures to check.

lessons.subject: Maths
lessons.title: Compass points, scale and coordinates
lessons.intention: We are learning to use eight compass points, maps with scales and coordinates.
criteria: I can use the eight compass points and their angles.
I can read maps and plans with simple scales, as in 1 cm : 2 km.
I can plot and describe points with coordinates in the first quadrant.

steps.start: Which direction is halfway between North and East?
steps.teach: Draw the eight compass points with angles between them. Measure on a map and use the scale. Plot (3, 5) and (5, 3) — along first, then up.
steps.practise: Angles and turns, then plot a shape from coordinates.
steps.check: On a 1 cm : 2 km map, 4·5 cm is how far? Plot (2, 6).

lessons.home: Use a map on a walk and work out real distances.
lessons.vocab: North-East, South-West, scale, coordinates, axis, plot
lessons.understand: On a scale of 1 cm to 2 km, how far is 3.5 cm?
lessons.lookFor: Multiplies by the scale: 7 km, and explains why.

lessons.subject: Maths
lessons.title: Lines of symmetry
lessons.intention: We are learning to find lines of symmetry and complete symmetrical patterns.
criteria: I can draw lines of symmetry on 2D shapes.
I can complete symmetrical pictures and patterns.

steps.start: How many lines of symmetry does a square have?
steps.teach: Fold and use mirrors to find lines of symmetry in regular and irregular shapes. Complete patterns on squared paper across vertical, horizontal and diagonal lines.
steps.practise: Complete three symmetrical patterns on squared paper.
steps.check: Draw the lines of symmetry on a rectangle and a regular hexagon.

lessons.home: Look for symmetry in flags, logos and leaves.
lessons.vocab: symmetry, line of symmetry, reflect, mirror line
lessons.understand: Does a rectangle have a diagonal line of symmetry? Prove it.
lessons.lookFor: Folds or reflects to show the halves don't match, so no.

lessons.subject: Maths
lessons.title: Graphs, pie charts and reliable data
lessons.intention: We are learning to collect, display and interpret data, and judge if it's reliable.
criteria: I can collect data in a suitable way.
I can display data in tables, bar graphs, line graphs, frequency tables and simple pie charts, with a suitable scale.
I can draw conclusions from data.
I can judge how reliable data is, thinking about who made it and the sample size.

steps.start: Is a survey of 3 people enough to know the favourite food of a whole school?
steps.teach: Make a frequency table, then a bar graph and a line graph for change over time. Read a simple pie chart. Spot a misleading graph scale.
steps.practise: Reading tables, then Bar charts.
steps.check: Read values from a line graph and explain one conclusion.

lessons.home: Look at a graph in the news: is it fair or misleading?
lessons.vocab: frequency table, line graph, pie chart, scale, reliable, sample
lessons.understand: Could this data be misleading? Why?
lessons.lookFor: Looks at the sample size, who collected it and the scale.

lessons.subject: Maths
lessons.title: Probability and chance experiments
lessons.intention: We are learning to describe probability and test it with experiments.
criteria: I can describe likelihood with equal chance, fifty-fifty, one in two, percentages and fractions like ⅙.
I can plan and carry out experiments with repeated trials.
I can use data to predict outcomes.

steps.start: What is the chance of rolling a 6? Of an even number?
steps.teach: Predict how many 6s in 30 rolls, then test it. Record results in a tally. Compare with the prediction and talk about why they differ.
steps.practise: How likely is it?
steps.check: A bag has 3 red and 1 blue counter. What is the chance of blue, as a fraction and a percentage?

lessons.home: Flip a coin 20 times and record heads and tails.
lessons.vocab: probability, chance, fifty-fifty, one in, likely, outcome, trial
lessons.understand: You flipped 4 heads in a row. Is tails more likely next? Why?
lessons.lookFor: Knows each flip is still an even chance: what happened before doesn't change it.

lessons.subject: Maths
lessons.title: Maths in inventions, life and work
lessons.intention: We are learning how maths shapes the world, now and in the past.
criteria: I can find and present examples of how maths is used in life and work.
I can discuss the part maths played in important inventions.

steps.start: Which jobs need maths? Which inventions needed it?
steps.teach: Choose an invention (bridges, computers, GPS) and find the maths it needs. Plan a short presentation.
steps.practise: Make a fact poster or slide about one example.
steps.check: Explain one way maths is used in a job you'd like.

lessons.home: Ask family members how they use maths at work or at home.
lessons.vocab: invention, engineer, data, measurement
lessons.understand: What maths would someone use in this job? Give an example.
lessons.lookFor: Names the maths (measuring, angles, money, data) and a real task it's used for.
